title: Houthis Capture Mocha in Push on Bab el-Mandeb as Saudi Output Hits 36-Year Low; Putin Brings Energy to Delhi BRICS
subhead: Iran-backed Houthis seized the Red Sea port of Mocha and Zuqar Island, advancing on Bab el-Mandeb, while data showed Saudi crude output plunged to its lowest since 1990. Putin's arrival in New Delhi for the BRICS summit puts energy and critical minerals at the center of India-Russia talks.

sections.heading: Houthis Seize Mocha, Open a Second Front on Bab el-Mandeb
sections.body:
Iran-backed Houthi forces captured the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha on Thursday, with a Yemeni military source telling AFP the rebels were advancing toward the Bab el-Mandeb strait 'after having taken control of Mocha.' Witnesses told AFP of fighters chanting 'death to America, death to Israel.' The Houthis also seized Zuqar Island in the southern Red Sea after what a military source described as rocket attacks and a seaborne ground assault, per France 24.

Advancing rebels are reportedly pushing toward the Hanish Islands and Perim Island, which command the Bab el-Mandeb southern approach, according to Times of India coverage. The Yemeni leader Rashad al-Alimi said protecting the country's coasts was now an 'Arab and international interest.' Saudi Arabia launched dozens of airstrikes in the past 24 hours, per the Houthi military spokesman.
sections.whyItMatters: This is a new theater in the chokepoint war: having tightened its grip on Hormuz traffic, Tehran's proxies are now working to replicate that squeeze at Bab el-Mandeb — the Red Sea outlet that Saudi Arabia has been diverting crude through since its Hormuz route was shut.

sections.heading: Saudi Output Slumps to 36-Year Low as Both Export Routes Are Cut
sections.body:
Saudi Arabia reported to OPEC that its August crude output fell by 1.9 million bpd to 6.238 million bpd — the kingdom's lowest production since 1990 — while exports plunged to 3.2 million bpd, the lowest in 13 years, per Bloomberg data cited by Al-Monitor and Kpler.

The collapse reflects a double squeeze: Riyadh diverted most crude to its East-West Pipeline and Red Sea port of Yanbu after the Strait of Hormuz shut, but in July the Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, and Kpler data cited by the New York Times shows only two Saudi cargoes passed through Bab el-Mandeb in the past week. Houthi strikes on Saudi facilities wounded 73 people on Tuesday, per Saudi authorities.
sections.whyItMatters: OPEC's de facto leader has lost access to both its primary export chokepoints simultaneously — an unprecedented bind that is removing spare capacity from the market while prices are already above $100.

sections.heading: Putin Lands in Delhi for BRICS as Energy and Minerals Top the Agenda
sections.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin touched down in New Delhi on Friday for the BRICS summit, his first overseas trip in this phase of the war, with bilateral talks with PM Modi scheduled on the sidelines, per Times of India. The Financial Express outlines an agenda covering Russian oil supplies, trade deficit, de-dollarisation and defence.

Indian industry coverage (Moneycontrol) reports New Delhi is looking to Russia to help plug gaps in critical minerals and rare earths as it steps up overseas sourcing, alongside a domestic push from exploration into processing and separation capability, reported by ET Energyworld.
sections.whyItMatters: As Western energy ties strain under sanctions, India is deepening a dual-track Russia relationship — discounted crude now, and critical-mineral supply chains for its green transition — at a moment when oil at $100-plus makes the economics of that discount far more attractive to Delhi.

sections.heading: US Moves on Kenya Minerals as Rare Earth Stocks Slide on Sino-US Thaw Hopes
sections.body:
The United States, through assistant secretary of state for Africa Frank Garcia, said it will help Kenya build mineral-processing factories, with one report pegging the proposed package at about $62 billion (8 trillion Kenyan shillings), focused on the Mrima Hill deposit expected to hold rare earths and niobium, per impactnews-wire and Reuters. Garcia said critical minerals are 'a top priority' for the Trump administration.

Separately, US rare earth stocks tumbled Thursday — USA Rare Earth down 4%, MP Materials down 5% — on hopes of a US-China thaw ahead of the Sept. 24 Trump-Xi meeting in Washington, per 247wallst. The move cuts against Washington's parallel push to fund domestic battery supply chains, including a reported $500 million directive to reduce US battery reliance on China.
sections.whyItMatters: Washington is simultaneously courting new processing partners in Africa and betting on diplomatic de-escalation with Beijing — two strategies whose market signals are pulling in opposite directions.

sections.heading: OPEC Cuts 2026 Demand Outlook for Fifth Straight Month
sections.body:
OPEC downgraded its 2026 oil demand growth forecast by 200,000 bpd to 380,000 bpd, leaving total consumption at 105.84 million bpd — a cumulative 1 million bpd cut since the US-Iran war began, per Argus's review of the latest Monthly Oil Market Report. The downgrade was driven by China and parts of the Asia-Pacific and Middle East. OPEC raised its 2027 growth forecast by 200,000 bpd to 2.36 million bpd, and held non-OPEC+ supply growth at 640,000 bpd for 2026.

This comes as a Reuters survey shows OPEC output itself fell in August, driven by Saudi export disruption — even as the producer group struggles with internal cohesion: the UAE left OPEC in May, and Iraq threatened in June to leave without a higher quota before PM Ali al-Zaidi affirmed in July that Baghdad would stay, per Al-Monitor.
sections.whyItMatters: For the first time in years, demand weakness and supply disruption are moving together — OPEC is trimming its demand view even as its own members cannot pump, a combination that leaves the market's price signal driven almost entirely by war risk.

sections.heading: Three of Five Tankers Sunk by US Were Tied to Russia's Shadow Fleet
sections.body:
Ukraine's sanctions commissioner Vladyslav Vlasiuk told Ukrinform that three of the five tankers struck by US forces on Sept. 8 — named as Kaviz, Charminar and Riesco — have direct links to Russia's shadow fleet. Vlasiuk said the Kaviz called at Ust-Luga and Novorossiysk and had a history of disabling its AIS tracking, and was linked to Fractal Marine DMCC, a company he describes as a key shadow-fleet operator; the Charminar is tied to a shipping network controlled by Iranian oil magnate Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani.

The claim, if confirmed, points to the deepening interpenetration of Russian and Iranian oil logistics — Iranian cargoes carried on vessels that also move Russian crude under sanctions.
sections.whyItMatters: The blurring between Iran's and Russia's evasive fleets complicates any attempt to sanction one without hitting the other, and shows the two sanctioned exporters are sharing tanker infrastructure to keep barrels moving.

bottomLine: The chokepoint war has opened a second front: the Houthis' capture of Mocha and Zuqar Island puts Bab el-Mandeb in play just as Saudi Arabia, already cut off from Hormuz, shows its Red Sea fallback is failing too — output at 6.238 million bpd is the lowest since 1990. With OPEC trimming its demand outlook even as supply is physically disrupted, oil's price signal is now pure war risk. Geopolitically, the ground is shifting away from the US and toward New Delhi, where Putin's BRICS arrival brings Russian crude and critical minerals onto the table just as Washington courts Kenya's rare earths and hopes a Trump-Xi thaw cools the metals market.
sources: France 24/AFP, Al-Monitor/Bloomberg/Kpler/NYT, Reuters, ArgusMedia, Ukrinform, Times of India, Financial Express, Moneycontrol, ET Energyworld, impactnews-wire, The Star Kenya, 247wallst, Washington Post, TimesNowNews, Outlook India
